topic: Valence Bond Theory and Orbital Overlap
title: Sigma and Pi Bonds Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A handshake, hook tape and a bicycle chain all grip only where two parts overlap. Atoms do the same. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we learn valence bond theory: a bond forms where two orbitals overlap.

On the molecule bench, two hydrogen atoms come closer while pulls and pushes act, and the energy curve dips to its lowest point at 74 pm, releasing 435.8 kJ/mol. Then we see positive, negative and zero overlap, head-on sigma bonds (s-s, s-p, p-p) and side by side pi bonds, count the bonds in single, double and triple bonds, and work out 5 sigma and 1 pi in ethene. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 47 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three grips, one idea
0:26 Where the shared electrons sit
0:57 The molecule bench: two H atoms meet
1:46 Positive, negative and zero overlap
2:25 Pause and think: sigma or pi?
2:39 The rules, link by link
3:14 Worked example: bonds in ethene
3:42 Sigma vs pi side by side
4:02 Exam trap: the triple bond
4:22 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:00 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Hybridisation. Carbon has only two half filled orbitals, so how does it make four equal bonds?

Video by Quest Academy.
